dedupe_keys.name: user request provisioning oriented slice anomaly prediction and resource allocation in 6g networks

description: The model predicts user requests and positions to identify potential network-slice anomalies while choosing resource allocations. The authors formulate the objective as maximizing long-term net promoter score under service-level requirements. Simulated comparisons report improved scores and lower average latency relative to baselines, without numerical effects in the abstract. This establishes a telecom service-provisioning model, not an observed customer-satisfaction dataset. The inspected metadata do not expose code, full network configurations, fitted parameters or deployment outcomes. The deposited documents or data declare CC BY 4.0 and public access. Geographic and temporal coverage remain bounded to explicitly named tests or locations, with other fields unknown. Only metadata was inspected, without reading measurements, archives, source code or document bodies. Related project reports may overlap; independent sample counts and equivalent test conditions are not assumed. This supports the source-defined communication system performance simulation role. Public paper access and licence do not establish executable availability, software rights or operating costs.
